findings.element: Try it on a sample payment outcome banner, In plain terms, the query disclosure, the Save button and the GSP Payment application chip — all while Apply payments to invoices is off
findings.finding: Every behavioural claim on the screen — including a positive Applied verdict on a named invoice — continues to render as live while the screen own banner declares the rule inert.
findings.user_impact: A user who turned the prerequisite off reads Applied to INV-1042 plus a green Custom rule chip, believes payments are now being matched to invoices, and leaves real payments unapplied and un-reconciled indefinitely.
findings.suggested_fix: While the prerequisite is off, render all three disclosures in an explicitly inert form — replace the simulator verdict with Nothing runs: Apply payments to invoices is off, prefix plain terms with Once it is on, Synder would…, retitle the query panel to would send — and make the GSP chip read Custom rule (inactive) in grey rather than green.

evidence.action: Turn Apply payments to invoices off on the GSP page, click Configure, leave the rule on with its default configuration, open Try it on a sample payment with the default card selected. Save, then look back at the GSP row.
evidence.observed: The inert-prerequisite warning and the verdict Applied — Applied to INV-1042. No invoice created. are both present on the same screen, with plain terms still asserting it applies the payment, and the footer reading Applies to Stripe — mzkt.by only. renderSim() gates only on validate() and never reads the prerequisite; the Save gate is errors plus plan only. The GSP row simultaneously shows the green Custom rule chip and the corrective text Turn on Apply payments to invoices first — the chip and the description of the same row disagree.

findings.element: Cancel sync toggle in section 3 of the overlay, against the identically named toggle in GSP integration settings
findings.finding: An existing, already-live production setting is presented as a single shared value but has two different commit semantics — instant on GSP, Save-gated and silently discardable in the overlay — and is uncommittable while the rule has a validation error.
findings.user_impact: A user who opens the overlay only to switch cancel-on-no-match off, sees the toggle read Off, and closes with Escape or Cancel walks away believing unmatched payments will now sync as usual, while Synder keeps cancelling them — or the mirror case.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the shared cancel-sync value immediately on click in the overlay too, independent of the rule draft and of the Save gate; if it must stay Save-gated, label it in place as a pending change and warn on Cancel/Escape that the shared setting will revert.

evidence.action: On GSP note Cancel sync reads Off. Click Configure, turn the rule on, in section 3 click Cancel sync so it reads On, then press Escape. Read the GSP row. Repeat but first turn the Customer row off without ticking inheritance so Save is disabled.
evidence.observed: After Escape the GSP row still reads Off — closeOverlay() only removes a class and never writes cfg back to saved, and no warning is shown, despite the changing it in either place changes both claim. In the validation-error variant the overlay toggle reads On while Save is disabled, leaving a displayed state with no path to become the real state.

findings.element: The exact request Synder will send to QuickBooks — the DocNumber line of the generated query
findings.finding: The disclosure that exists specifically to prove what will be sent prints DocNumber = 'INV-1042' for every source setting and even for configurations whose clause the engine would drop.
findings.user_impact: A user verifying a rule that matches an order reference in the invoice note reads a query filtering on the invoice number, concludes the rule is wrong (or right) for the opposite reason, and ships a matcher that silently applies payments to the wrong invoices or to none.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the previewed literal from the same resolve() call the engine uses, state the sample payment value for the selected source in the preamble, and when the source resolves to absent replace the DocNumber line with an explicit clause dropped note.

evidence.action: Open the query disclosure, then change Take the value from through Invoice note, Invoice id, Subscription id, Payment note and Payment metadata; separately set the source to Payment metadata and clear the Metadata key.
evidence.observed: The DocNumber line stays DocNumber = 'INV-1042' for every source — sqlPreview() computes it from a dead ternary whose two branches are the same string — while run() builds the clause from resolve(). With the metadata key blank the query still shows the clause even though resolve() returns absent and the engine logs clause dropped.

findings.element: Section 2 condition row with operand is empty / is not empty: the greyed-out On the invoice select, the still-active On the payment select, and the matching In plain terms line
findings.finding: For is empty rows the UI disables the control that decides the check and leaves enabled the control that silently decides whether the row runs at all, and the plain-terms read-back describes only the disabled one.
findings.user_impact: A user builds apply to the invoice whose memo on statement is empty, reads back exactly that, and does not learn that on simple charges the condition is silently dropped, so the payment falls through to no matching open invoice and is either cancelled or posted unapplied.
findings.suggested_fix: For value-less operands, enable On the invoice and hide or neutralise On the payment (skipping its resolve() and its metadata-key validation), and have plain terms state the invoice field being tested with no payment-side dependency.

evidence.action: Set On the payment to Payment metadata with key invoices, set Comparison to is empty, read the row and In plain terms; open the simulator and select Reference not in the books (FDD example C), whose payment metadata is empty.
evidence.observed: On the invoice renders disabled while On the payment stays enabled; testOp() for empty tests only the invoice-side value; run() resolves the payment source first and logs row skipped, not applicable for that sample, and plainTerms() emits only the invoice memo is empty with no mention of the source that caused the skip.

gaps: overlay Cancel-sync toggle: the state map records it only as toggled in place, never toggled-then-closed-via-Cancel/Escape, so the discard behaviour is read from the handler rather than an exercised interaction

admin no-date-limit entitlement revocation silently forces the date row back on; revocation against an already-saved rule was never exercised, so whether the user is told their saved rule was narrowed is unknown
post-save acknowledgement: Save closes the overlay with no toast; no failed-save path exists in the prototype, so error and rollback behaviour on a real commit is unverified
In plain terms never mentions the inheritance flag, so with Customer off the read-back is silent on customer attribution for a matched payment
the query preview sample payment is hardcoded and unrelated to the user data; whether production intends real-data substitution determines how much of TRU-3 survives into shipped code
Starter plan: reaching the overlay on Starter was never exercised, so whether a Starter user can open, edit and attempt to save a rule is unverified
